HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which tree is also called the peepal? (1 mark)
   A. Ber tree
   B. Tulsi
   C. Bodhi tree
   D. Sal tree

2. Which is a good way to save water? (1 mark)
   A. Close the tap fully after use
   B. Wash the car every day
   C. Leave taps running
   D. Pour water on the road

3. Which activity shows how to care for the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing rubbish out of a matatu
   B. Planting a tree in the school compound
   C. Cutting trees for fun
   D. Burning waste in the field

4. What should you do when you join a religious activity of another faith? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at it
   B. Listen carefully and behave politely
   C. Refuse to sit
   D. Make noise

5. Which element is called Prithvi? (1 mark)
   A. Earth
   B. Fire
   C. Water
   D. Air

6. What did Siddhartha do for the wounded swan? (1 mark)
   A. He took it away to eat
   B. He pulled out the arrow and nursed it
   C. He ignored it
   D. He shot it again

7. From where did Narsimha appear in the story? (1 mark)
   A. The sky at noon
   B. A boat
   C. A pillar in the palace
   D. A river

8. What is an Avtar? (1 mark)
   A. A holy river
   B. A form in which God is believed to come to earth
   C. A daily prayer
   D. A kind of tree

9. Sri Guru Ram Das Ji was which Guru of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. The fourth
   B. The tenth
   C. The first
   D. The third

10. What did Bharat place on the throne? (1 mark)
   A. Ram's sandals (paduka)
   B. A crown
   C. A book
   D. A lamp

11. Who was the king of Ayodhya in the Ramayan? (1 mark)
   A. Dasharatha
   B. Hiranyakashipu
   C. Harishchandra
   D. Suddhodana

12. What is the lesson of Bharat refusing the throne? (1 mark)
   A. Never obey
   B. Grab wealth
   C. Take what you like
   D. Be humble and do not be greedy for power

13. According to the Dhammapada teachings in the lesson, hatred is ended by what? (1 mark)
   A. Silence
   B. More hatred
   C. Fighting
   D. Love

14. Who was Sigala? (1 mark)
   A. A Sikh Guru
   B. A Jain monk
   C. A king of Ayodhya
   D. A young man taught by the Buddha

15. What does Ik Onkar stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Many rivers
   B. Two gods
   C. Six directions
   D. There is one God

16. In Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva, whom does the prayer speak to? (1 mark)
   A. A tree
   B. A king
   C. God
   D. A river

17. What greeting shows respect with folded hands? (1 mark)
   A. Sat Sri Akal
   B. Hujambo
   C. Shalom
   D. Namaste

18. What is a prayer? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A way of talking to God
   C. A sport
   D. A kind of meal

19. What did King Harishchandra give up rather than break his promise? (1 mark)
   A. His kingdom
   B. His lamp
   C. His shoes
   D. His horse

20. What does it mean to pay your fare honestly? (1 mark)
   A. Pay the right amount and take your change
   B. Avoid paying
   C. Hide from the conductor
   D. Pay less

21. Which action during the journey is wrong? (1 mark)
   A. Putting hands out of the window
   B. Sitting still
   C. Speaking quietly
   D. Keeping the aisle clear

22. Which is a mistake in yoga practice? (1 mark)
   A. Following the teacher
   B. Wearing loose clothes
   C. Being calm
   D. Comparing yourself with others

23. What does Kapaal Bhaati mean? (1 mark)
   A. Moon pose
   B. Sitting pose
   C. Diamond pose
   D. Shining forehead

24. What does Pranayam mean? (1 mark)
   A. Prayer
   B. Song
   C. Breathing exercise
   D. Body posture

25. Why is yoga best done with an expert? (1 mark)
   A. To be noisy
   B. So no one else can join
   C. To finish faster
   D. To avoid strain from wrong posture

26. Why should Kapaal Bhaati and Bhastrika be done gently by children? (1 mark)
   A. They are active and need care
   B. They are painful always
   C. They are very slow
   D. They cannot be done

27. Which is an activity for International Yoga Day? (1 mark)
   A. Doing yoga together at school or a park
   B. Staying at home only
   C. Skipping class
   D. Playing loud music

28. In which year was International Yoga Day first celebrated? (1 mark)
   A. 2015
   B. 2030
   C. 2005
   D. 1990

29. What does the Vedic saying say about the truth? (1 mark)
   A. It has many separate truths
   B. It is one but is called by many names
   C. It is unknown
   D. It is only for kings

30. What does Punarjanam mean? (1 mark)
   A. A prayer
   B. A river
   C. Rebirth
   D. A festival

31. On which date did Kenya become fully independent? (1 mark)
   A. 1 June 1963
   B. 21 June 2015
   C. 1 January 1964
   D. 12 December 1963

32. What does the Kiswahili word Madaraka mean? (1 mark)
   A. Freedom of religion
   B. Food
   C. Peace
   D. Power or authority to govern

33. Which festival in the lesson is celebrated near the middle of the year on 1 June? (1 mark)
   A. Yoga Day
   B. Maha Shivratri
   C. Paryushan
   D. Madaraka Day

34. What is Paryushan Parva mainly about? (1 mark)
   A. Feasts only
   B. Prayer, self-control and forgiveness
   C. Wealth
   D. Racing

35. What does Micchami Dukkadam mean? (1 mark)
   A. Good morning
   B. May any harm I did be forgiven
   C. Happy birthday
   D. Thank you for the food

36. What is done to the Shiva Linga on Maha Shivratri? (1 mark)
   A. It is covered
   B. It is thrown in a river
   C. It is bathed with water and milk
   D. It is painted red

37. What does fasting on Maha Shivratri show? (1 mark)
   A. Self-control
   B. Anger
   C. Greed
   D. Laziness

38. What is the Indian name for Tuesday? (1 mark)
   A. Shukravaar
   B. Mangalvaar
   C. Somvaar
   D. Ravivaar

39. What is the Indian name for Saturday? (1 mark)
   A. Ravivaar
   B. Shanivaar
   C. Mangalvaar
   D. Guruvaar

40. Budh is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Jupiter
   B. Saturn
   C. Mercury
   D. Mars

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name the three prayers studied in this lesson. (2 marks)

42. Write a weekly plan using English and Indian day names with one activity for each of three days. (5 marks)

43. Explain how the school can plan a tree planting day that includes learners with special needs. (5 marks)

44. What is Dharma? (2 marks)

45. Why should we breathe slowly during asanas? (2 marks)

46. Explain how you can show integrity when using the internet. (3 marks)

47. Explain what the white colour, the veena and the book stand for in the picture of Saraswati. (3 marks)

48. Explain the main teachings of the Dhammapada. (3 marks)

49. Give three uses of the Indian traditional calendar. (3 marks)

50. State three contributions of Sri Guru Ram Das Ji. (3 marks)

51. Explain why forgiveness is important, using Paryushan Parva. (4 marks)

52. What does the name Narsimha mean? (2 marks)

53. What is a festival? (2 marks)

54. Describe the snake story of Lord Parshvanath. (3 marks)

55. Distinguish between Madaraka Day and Jamhuri Day. (3 marks)

56. Name any four of the five great elements of the Panch Mahabhoot. (2 marks)

57. What is a Tirthankar? (2 marks)

58. Explain how a maize farm uses all five elements. (4 marks)

59. Name two grahas in the traditional calendar that are not planets in modern science. (2 marks)

60. Explain why water is important in our daily lives. (3 marks)

61. What is the essence of a scripture? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Bodhi tree
   The Bodhi tree is a kind of fig tree, also called the peepal.

2. A — Close the tap fully after use
   Closing taps stops waste.

3. B — Planting a tree in the school compound
   Planting trees helps the environment.

4. B — Listen carefully and behave politely
   We show respect to all faiths.

5. A — Earth
   Prithvi is the Sanskrit word for earth, the soil and rocks.

6. B — He pulled out the arrow and nursed it
   He helped the hurt bird.

7. C — A pillar in the palace
   The pillar broke open and he appeared.

8. B — A form in which God is believed to come to earth
   An Avtar is a coming down of God to protect goodness.

9. A — The fourth
   He came after Guru Amar Das Ji.

10. A — Ram's sandals (paduka)
   Bharat ruled in Ram's name.

11. A — Dasharatha
   King Dasharatha ruled Ayodhya.

12. D — Be humble and do not be greedy for power
   He knew the throne belonged to Ram.

13. D — Love
   Hatred is not ended by hatred but by love.

14. D — A young man taught by the Buddha
   The talk was given to him.

15. D — There is one God
   Ik Onkar means One God.

16. C — God
   It speaks to God as parent and friend.

17. D — Namaste
   Namaste is done with folded hands.

18. B — A way of talking to God
   We thank God and ask for wisdom.

19. A — His kingdom
   He gave up his whole kingdom.

20. A — Pay the right amount and take your change
   Honesty includes paying fares.

21. A — Putting hands out of the window
   Hands can be hurt.

22. D — Comparing yourself with others
   Yoga is not a competition.

23. D — Shining forehead
   Kapaal is forehead and bhaati is shining.

24. C — Breathing exercise
   Pranayam is control of the breath.

25. D — To avoid strain from wrong posture
   Experts correct mistakes.

26. A — They are active and need care
   They are active exercises.

27. A — Doing yoga together at school or a park
   People do yoga together.

28. A — 2015
   It was first celebrated in 2015.

29. B — It is one but is called by many names
   The truth is one, the wise call it by many names.

30. C — Rebirth
   Punarjanam is being born again.

31. D — 12 December 1963
   Jamhuri Day is 12 December.

32. D — Power or authority to govern
   It means authority to govern.

33. D — Madaraka Day
   1 June is mid-year.

34. B — Prayer, self-control and forgiveness
   These are its main themes.

35. B — May any harm I did be forgiven
   It is a plea for forgiveness.

36. C — It is bathed with water and milk
   This is called abhishek.

37. A — Self-control
   It teaches self-control.

38. B — Mangalvaar
   Mangal is Mars.

39. B — Shanivaar
   Shani is Saturn.

40. C — Mercury
   Budh is Mercury.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gayatri Mantra, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva and Saraswati Vandana (any correct pair earns 1 mark).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark each, rounded up.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct plan, for example Somvaar: help at home; Guruvaar: thank a teacher; Shukravaar: share with a friend.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the format and 1 mark each for three correct day names with activities.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a suitable place and get permission, prepare seedlings, tools and water, and give each child a job they can do, such as holding seedlings, filling watering cans or drawing the plants. Care for the trees afterwards.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for permission, preparing, jobs for all, inclusion of special needs, and continued care.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: The right way of living, including duty, honesty and kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for two ideas.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us calm and helps the body relax.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission before using a device, do not copy another's work, do not send unkind or untrue messages, and keep personal details private (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: White stands for purity and peace, the veena stands for music and the arts, and the book stands for knowledge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Our thoughts shape our actions, hatred is ended by love, control of anger is strength, and doing good brings peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each teaching, up to 3.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fixing festival dates, choosing days for prayers and family events, keeping tradition alive (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: He started the city of Amritsar and the Sarovar, composed hymns and the Laavan, and taught equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each contribution.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Forgiveness removes anger, mends friendships and brings peace. On the last day Jains ask everyone for forgiveness with Micchami Dukkadam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Man-lion, from nar (man) and simha (lion).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: A special day or set of days when people come together to remember something important.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for special day and 1 mark for remembering or celebrating together.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: A man was burning a log. Parshvanath saw that a snake was inside and asked him to stop. The snake was saved, and the man learned a lesson about kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the log, 1 mark for the snake, 1 mark for the rescue or lesson.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day is 1 June and marks internal self-government in 1963. Jamhuri Day is 12 December and marks independence in 1963 and the republic in 1964.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each date and 1 mark for a difference.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: Prithvi (earth), Jal (water), Agni (fire), Vayu (air), Akash (space).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each correct element, up to 2 marks.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: A Jain teacher who shows people the path to freedom, like a guide across a river.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for teacher, 1 mark for showing the path.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: The soil is Prithvi, rain and river water are Jal, the sun's heat is Agni, the wind that carries pollen is Vayu, and the open sky is Akash.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for each element linked correctly to the farm, up to 4.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Sun and the Moon.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is needed for drinking and cooking, for washing and cleaning, and for growing crops and giving drinks to animals. Without it people, animals and plants cannot live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The most important message or lesson in it.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct meaning.
